notes:
Summary: Crestfall is evaluating Redwood Dedicated for latency-sensitive personalization + chat at scale. Primary ask: predictable monthly cost with throughput guarantees and clear per-token economics under committed capacity. Key stakeholders: CTO (H. Rivera), Head of ML Eng (S. Patel), VP Product (M. O'Neill).

Key requirements / asks (shorthand):
- 95th pct latency SLO: p95 < 120ms for short-chat (<=512 tokens), p95 < 250ms for 2k seq reranking paths.
- Throughput guarantees: sustained 25k tokens/sec across peak pool; spike handling to 40k tokens/sec for 10m bursts.
- Reserved GPU planning: prefer 8-12 x A100-80GB for baseline; want option to swap in H100 for heavy quant workloads.
- SLA negotiation points: credits for missed latency SLOs (10% monthly credit per missed SLO tier), fallback policy to hosted for DR, 48-hour notice for maintenance windows.

Cost-model discussion notes (from SE + AE):
- Redwood proposal v2 modeled two commit tiers: "Conservative" = 4x A100 reserved; "Production" = 12x A100 reserved. Monthly committed cost assumptions used in deck: $30k/mo (4x A100), $85k/mo (12x A100) -- includes reserved GPU node fee + base infra + support tier. These are placeholders; still negotiating.
- Utilization assumptions: Crestfall requested modeling at 30% avg util (steady state) and 60% avg util (improved demand) for token-level unit economics. SE note: effective util = active GPU cycles consumed after batching & KV cache savings.
- Token throughput per A100 (assumption): ~250k tokens/sec-equivalent throughput per GPU when heavily batched for embeddings; for chat with low-latency continuous batching assume ~20-40k tokens/sec per GPU depending on seq length and model family.

Example unit economics (worksheet excerpts paraphrased):
- Production commit (12x A100, $85k/mo) at 30% util -> effective cost per 1k tokens = $0.95; at 60% util -> $0.48 per 1k tokens.
- Conservative commit (4x A100, $30k/mo) at 30% util -> $1.20 per 1k tokens; at 60% util -> $0.60 per 1k tokens.
- Embeddings workload (dense batching) shows best-case ~0.12 per 1k tokens due to higher batching and cheaper model variants.
- Notes: these numbers include amortized reserved capacity + estimated ops + infra overhead but exclude customer-specific savings from prefix caching and model quantization (Optimize recommendations could reduce these by additional 15-35%).

Negotiation items to surface to Finance / Legal:
- Define exact credit formula for SLA misses (latency and availability separated).
- Agree gamma on committed months / early termination (12 vs 24 month options).
- GPU SKU substitution clause (H100 fallback, pricing parity or uplift?).

POC plan (short):
- Week 1-2: traffic replay to dedicated mini-pool (2-4 GPUs) to validate latency distribution and offline utilization metrics.
- Week 3: scale to target commit slice (8 GPUs) and test burst behavior; run stress tests against routing fallback to hosted.
- Deliverable: unit-economics model v3 with measured tokens/sec per node, KV cache hit ratio, and adjusted per-1k token costs.

Direct quotes / paraphrases from customers: "We need a predictable monthly line item we can model into ops — if utilization varies, we need visibility and clear fallbacks." "Finance will only greenlight if ARR breakeven < 18 months at our conservative estimates."
unit_economics_summary: Two-tier model delivered to customer: conservative (4x A100) and production (12x A100). Key drivers: commit price, realized utilization, batching/KV cache hit rates, model family. Example outputs: $0.95/1k tokens at 30% util on 12x A100; potential down to $0.48/1k with 60% util and Optimize-led quantization. Embeddings significantly cheaper due to dense batching (~$0.12/1k in best-case).
